attributes.context: The clause is located in Article 4, Section 4.1, concerning labor-management committee meetings. It follows a list of discussion items, including impact on staff reductions, and is followed by a sentence stating that information about work stations not meeting CBA provisions will be forwarded to City-wide committees to set a timetable for replacement.

extraction_text: It is the further understanding of the parties that discussion of the addition and replacement of VDT work stations to conform with the provisions set forth in the collective bargaining agreement will take place at departmental labor-management and health and safety committee meetings.

attributes.context: The surrounding chunk appoints a joint Union-Employer committee of mutually agreed equal representatives and requires it to meet at reasonable intervals to study career ladders, semi-automatic progression, training, salary grade placements, and Avant Job Series groupings affected by computerization of clerical jobs.
The clause appears under Section 19.3 - Video Display Terminals (VDT) and is immediately followed by an accommodation requirement for pregnant or nursing employees who normally operate VDTs.

extraction_text: VDT work stations, as they are added or replaced within the discretion of the Employer, shall contain glare screens, chairs with adjustable heights and back rests, foot rests and adjustable tables for holding keyboards.

attributes.context: This is item 1 in Side Letter 23, which confirms agreements reached during the 1999-2000 contract negotiations between the City of Chicago and AFSCME Council 31.

extraction_text: Semi-automatic progression: The City of Chicago and the Union will form a committee to examine the feasibility and possible implementation of a pilot program for semi-automatic progression for the following job titles -- Sanitarian I to Sanitarian II (Health Department); Auditor I to Auditor II (Revenue Department); and Fingerprint Technician I to II (Police Department).
